findings.reason: The diff deletes the `if (opts.flowSkipColonSpace) opts.quoteFlowKeys = true` guard from createPresenterState, and nothing else turns quoting on: styler_defaults.ts:33 quotes keys only when quoteFlowKeys is set. writeFlowMapping (presenter.ts:215,223) sets sep to '' and writes `a:1`. The parser at parser.ts:807-809 ends a plain scalar at ':' only when whitespace, end of input or a flow indicator follows, so `a:1` is read as one key with no value. Trigger: the dump call above, then load(). Both reviewers traced it the same way.
findings.claim: With flowSkipColonSpace on, the change no longer forces quoteFlowKeys, so dump({a:1},{flowLevel:0,flowSkipColonSpace:true}) writes '{a:1}', and loading that gives {'a:1': null}. The data no longer survives a dump and load.
findings.evidence: The diff deletes `if (opts.flowSkipColonSpace) { opts.quoteFlowKeys = true }` from `createPresenterState`, and nothing else adds that protection back. `writeFlowMapping` (presenter.ts:215,223) sets `sep = state.flowSkipColonSpace ... ? '' : ' '` and writes `${keyText}:${sep}${valueText}`, which gives `a:1`. In the parser, the plain-scalar reader (src/parser/parser.ts:807-809) only stops at `:` when the next character is whitespace, end of line, end of input or a flow indicator (in flow context). A `1` is none of these, so the key scalar reads as `a:1` and the mapping entry gets no value. The removed doc comment said this was the reason for the guard: "otherwise `a:1` would be parsed as a single plain scalar instead of a mapping entry". Trigger: `dump({a: 1}, {flowLevel: 0, flowSkipColonSpace: true})`, then `load` the result.

findings.reason: Line 154 does compare text only, but this file is not in the diff. Under acceptance.md it is one of the locked baseline tests, so this change cannot alter it. The weak test is a fault in the acceptance suite, not in this change. The test pins the output that C1 shows is broken, which is worth raising with whoever owns the story.
findings.claim: The flowSkipColonSpace test compares only the output text '{a:1}' and never loads it back.
findings.evidence: `assert.equal(dump({ a: 1 }, { flowLevel: 0, flowSkipColonSpace: true }), '{a:1}\n')` compares text only. The test for the neighbouring `quoteFlowKeys` option (lines 161-164) does check a round trip with `assert.deepEqual(load(output), { [key]: 1 })`. This test has no such check, so nothing verifies that `{a:1}` loads as `{a: 1}`, which it does not.

findings.reason: Line 36 is `it.skip(...)`, but the file is not in the diff, so the test was already skipped before this change. That gap in coverage is not something this change introduced.
findings.claim: The round-trip property test that covers flowSkipColonSpace is skipped.
findings.evidence: `it.skip('Load from dumped should be the original object', ...)` generates `flowSkipColonSpace: fc.boolean()` and asserts `deepStrictEqual(load(yamlContent), obj)`, but it is skipped, so it never runs against this change.

findings.reason: CHANGELOG.md has no entry for this change. It also has no Unreleased section, and its entries are dated release blocks, so the project may write entries only at release time. The code does not settle whether this change needed one. docs/migrate_v4_to_v5.md:184 only maps condenseFlow to the options and does not describe the forced quoting.
findings.claim: flowSkipColonSpace used to produce quoted keys and now produces unquoted ones, and there is no changelog entry for it.
findings.evidence: The diff touches only src/ast/presenter.ts: it removes the forced `quoteFlowKeys` and rewrites the option's JSDoc. CHANGELOG.md and docs/migrate_v4_to_v5.md:184, which maps `condenseFlow` to these options, are unchanged.
